problem_statement: wrappixel/Flexy-admin-Nextjs-Free (rebranded here as the Freightline fulfillment-operations dashboard) is a Next.js 12 Pages Router admin template built with MUI 5, Emotion, and ApexCharts. A fixed sidebar, top app bar, Shipment Volume chart, Daily Activity timeline, Warehouse Throughput table, and blog cards live under a shared FullLayout that wraps every route. Extend the console with a shared 'Fulfillment focus' filter card that rides above the page content across the operator's key routes. The card reuses the dashboard's OWN Warehouse Throughput rows (the same operators, projects, priorities, and budgets the Warehouse Throughput table is built from) behind a native priority-status chip filter (All / Low / Medium / High / Critical) over a card grid, with a live 'Showing N of M · <status>' readout inside the card. Clicking a chip filters the grid and recomputes the readout. It must render inside the existing FullLayout shell on the dashboard home, the Warehouse Throughput table page, and the about desk so the same operator surface follows the user, must adopt the native Flexy card language (teal accent, soft-shadow card surfaces, tinted tile panels), must stay overflow-free on a 390px phone while staying intact at 834px and 1440px, and its status chips must keep the readout in sync with the active filter. The surrounding chart, timeline, table, blog cards, sidebar, and app bar must remain unchanged in content and structure.
required_content: A shared 'Fulfillment focus' filter card renders inside the existing FullLayout on the dashboard home, the Warehouse Throughput table page (/table), and the about desk (/about), so the same card appears across multiple admin routes rather than on a single page.

The card presents a status-chip row (All / Low / Medium / High / Critical) over a grid built from the dashboard's OWN Warehouse Throughput rows (Sunil Joshi · Elite Admin, Andrew McDownland · Real Homes WP Theme, Christopher Jamil · MedicalPro WP Theme, Nirav Joshi · Hosting Press HTML), each tile showing the operator, project, role · priority · budget.
A live readout inside the card reads 'Showing N of M · <status>' and updates to reflect the current filtered count and active status; clicking a chip filters the grid AND recomputes the readout.

The card adopts the Flexy MUI visual system (7px rounded card surfaces, the template soft shadow, tinted tile panels, teal accent, muted helper text) and does not introduce an off-brand dark slate or neon palette.

On a 390px mobile viewport the chip row and card grid stay inside the viewport without causing horizontal page overflow; chips and tiles wrap or shrink rather than forcing the document wider than the screen. At 834px and 1440px the card lays out cleanly with no overflow.
The Shipment Volume chart, Daily Activity timeline, Warehouse Throughput table, blog cards, sidebar, and top app bar remain present and unchanged in content and structure.
design_constraints: Render the filter card through the shared FullLayout so it appears consistently across the whitelisted admin routes; do not paste a separate copy per page or hang it off a standalone route.
Keep the card in Flexy's restrained admin language: 7px rounded surfaces, the template soft shadow, tinted #f6f9fc tile panels, teal #03c9d7 accents, small muted helper text.
Do not introduce a new global palette (no off-brand dark slate / neon recolor of the card) or an external icon/chart library beyond the repo's existing setup.

The chip row and card grid must stay scannable and must not overflow the page horizontally on mobile; use fluid/wrapping chips and tiles rather than fixed wide non-wrapping cells, and do not mask the spill with body/html-level overflow clipping.

Clicking a status chip must update both the active chip state and the readout together; the readout must not freeze on its initial value after interaction. Keep the Next.js Pages Router build pipeline intact.
state_constraints: The shared Fulfillment focus filter card must render on the dashboard home, the /table throughput page, and the /about desk, and be captured as the main before/after evidence.
The card's mobile chip row and grid (mobile_home, mobile_rail_home at 390px) must be captured to confirm no horizontal page overflow after the fix.
The status-filter interaction state (desktop_rail_scope) must be captured after clicking the Low chip to confirm the grid filters and the readout re-syncs to 'Showing 1 of 4 · Low'.
The /forms route is a regression anchor where the card is intentionally absent (not on the whitelist) and its shell must not be restyled off-brand to satisfy the task.
All card content must be inspectable as React/Next DOM, not flattened into screenshots or hidden offscreen.

change_completion: A shared Fulfillment focus filter card is added through FullLayout and appears on the dashboard home, /table, and /about routes.

The card carries a status-chip row (All / Low / Medium / High / Critical) over a grid built from the dashboard's own Warehouse Throughput rows, with a live 'Showing N of M · status' readout inside the card.
Clicking a status chip filters the grid AND recomputes the readout to the active status after interaction.
design_consistency: The card uses Flexy card, shadow, typography, teal-accent, and spacing conventions and stays subordinate to the dashboard hierarchy.
The card keeps the native light palette and does not recolor into an off-brand dark slate or neon block.
The card reads as a refined admin workflow surface reusing the app's own table rows rather than a pasted marketing/analytics section.
responsive: At 390px the chip row and card grid wrap or flex down so the document width stays within the viewport.
At 834px and 1440px the card lays the chips and tiles in a balanced grid above the page content with no overflow.
regression: Shipment Volume chart, Daily Activity timeline, Warehouse Throughput table, blog cards, sidebar, and top app bar remain present and unchanged.
No new console errors or failed network requests appear on any captured state.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Flexy (wrappixel Flexy-admin-Nextjs-Free) Next.js 12 Pages Router MUI dashboard design-continuity restyle. The shared Fulfillment focus filter card is rendered through the existing FullLayout across the dashboard, throughput table, and about routes, reusing the dashboard's OWN Warehouse Throughput rows behind a native priority-status chip filter with a live count readout, in Flexy's rounded-card, teal-accent, muted-helper design language and the repo's local logo and background image assets. This task tests whether an agent can extend an existing admin workflow with a consistent cross-page filter over the app's own data in the native visual system, keep it responsive and overflow-free at 390/834/1440px, and wire the status chips so the grid filters and the readout stays in sync, rather than appending an off-brand section, dropping the card from secondary routes, or leaving a stale readout. Built with next build + next start; three legs differ only in the filter-card component, its stylesheet, and the FullLayout route whitelist.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Flexy-admin-Nextjs-Free is a runnable Next.js 12 Pages Router MUI dashboard template rebranded to the Freightline fulfillment-operations console; a newly added metrics strip introduces a mobile horizontal-overflow regression, making it an ideal host for a repair/state_continuity task whose sole discriminator is no_horizontal_overflow with content and DOM held identical across legs.
